clue.text: Rock turning to fragments: new pictures

indicators.note: turning tells us to read the nickname for Gibraltar from right to left

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, abbreviated GIB
scree is a mass of broken rock fragments on a slope

explanation.surface: A geologist watches a boulder crumble into shards and calls it something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses GIB to give BIG. 'Pictures' in the sense of 'going to the pictures' is the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: The cinema is called the pictures in British speech, and the cinema screen is its emblem, as opposed to television.

clue.text: Cleaner shrub

definitions.meaning: a sweeping implement with a long handle used for cleaning floors
a yellow-flowered leguminous bush of heathland, Cytisus

explanation.definitionFit: The sweeping implement and the yellow-flowered heathland bush share one name, the bush having once supplied the twigs for the brush.

clue.text: G-give job back for fruit

parts.note: the stammered G- of the clue supplies its letter
to give someone their job back is to take them on again, re-engage

explanation.surface: A stammering employer asks for a sacked worker to be rehired in exchange for some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'G-give' provides a lone G before RE-ENGAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a kind of green plum, a soft stone fruit.

clue.text: Father Christmas notes the Guardian's death warrant to privatisation

parts.note: Santa Claus, so CLAUS
E is a musical note
F is a second musical note
the setter's newspaper speaking of itself would say 'our'

explanation.surface: A newspaper notes that Santa has signed the death warrant for selling off state industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian, where the puzzle appeared, refers to itself as 'our'. 'Notes' gives two notes, E and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour's constitutional commitment to common ownership of industry stood squarely against selling state assets until Blair rewrote it in 1995.

clue.text: Railway cut short road in place of 1 across

parts.note: EL is the American elevated railway

indicators.note: cut short says the last letter of the word for road is dropped

parts.note: a street is a town road

explanation.surface: A railway line is truncated where a road crosses it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the final T of STREET. Elstree in Hertfordshire is home to famous British film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree is the home of well-known British film studios, so it is a home of the cinema.

clue.text: Kin to engineers being eaten by kine

indicators.note: something eaten by another goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: kine is an old plural of cow, and neat is an old word for cattle
RE is the Royal Engineers, here pluralised as RES

explanation.surface: Relatives of some engineers are being devoured by cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being eaten by' puts the engineers inside the kine. Kine and neat are both archaic words for cattle; 'kin' is a teasing echo of 'kine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Your nearest are your closest relatives, as in the phrase nearest and dearest.

clue.text: In which good shots come out with boodle and girl, and poor with hearse

definitions.text: In which good shots come out with boodle and girl

indicators.note: taken loosely, with here suggests the two words are mixed together into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film where the sharpshooters ride off with the loot and the heroine, and the bad shots leave in a coffin.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of POOR and HEARSE are rearranged; 'with' is a weak signal for this. 'Boodle' is slang for loot.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse opera is a facetious name for a cowboy film, where the hero gets the money and the girl.

clue.text: Defence? You must be joking!

definitions.meaning: a sunken ditch or fence that keeps livestock off a lawn without spoiling the view
an exclamation of mocking laughter at a silly suggestion

explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha is a hidden ditch serving as a boundary barrier, and ha ha is derisive laughter.

clue.text: Moving part will make gold perish

parts.note: to rot is to decay or perish
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A moving part made of gold is bound to perish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the revolving component of a machine such as a helicopter or engine.

clue.text: Pleasure-seeking but heartless film no Scots get upset about

indicators.note: about says the reversed Scots word goes round the shortened film
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the Scots word is read backwards

parts.note: nae is Scots for no

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letter of the word for film is removed

parts.note: a picture is a film

explanation.surface: A hedonist rejects a soulless film that the Scots dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the central T of PICTURE to give PICURE; 'get upset' turns NAE into EAN, which goes 'about' PICURE as E...AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean devotes themself to refined sensual enjoyment, especially of food and drink.

clue.text: See 6
Junction where Brits get back with Italian 6 9

parts.note: Spaghetti Junction is the nickname of a tangled motorway interchange in Birmingham
we, as the British speaking of ourselves
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: At a road interchange British drivers turn back, while an Italian makes a cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: Spaghetti Junction is a famous motorway interchange near Birmingham, England. 'where' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Westerns made by Italian directors such as Sergio Leone were nicknamed for the Italian staple food.

clue.text: Short run on 22 part 1 at home among sorrows

indicators.note: among says one piece is set within the letters of another

parts.note: miseries are sorrows
IN means at home

explanation.surface: A brief series on the television arrives at home amid sadness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' places the 'at home' letters inside the sorrows, after the M. 22's first part is BOX, British slang for the television.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniseries is a television drama shown in a small number of episodes, so a short run on the box.

clue.text: 4 due to give tongue

indicators.note: to give means the words yield up only the run of letters inside them, with the outer letters discarded

parts.note: with the figure 4 written out as the word four, the letters run on into due

explanation.surface: Four people are due to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: This is really a hidden word: write 4 as FOUR and the language sits across 'foUR DUe', so 'to give' drops the outer F, O and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a language, a tongue, spoken in Pakistan and India.

clue.text: Writer's one among teachers to put another type of 9 head to tail

definitions.text: another type of 9 head to tail

parts.note: a pen is a writer's instrument

indicators.note: among says one piece is put inside the letters of another

parts.note: schoolchildren call their male teachers sir
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer puts one among the teachers and turns another type of show upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself a puzzle: another opera is SOAP, and moving its S from head to tail gives OAPS, old age pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving the first letter of a soap to the end gives OAPs, the British abbreviation for old age pensioners.

clue.text: Pinch a bit

definitions.meaning: to pinch is to steal or grab something
a simple jointed mouthpiece for a horse

explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is slang for stealing, and a snaffle is a light horse's bit.

clue.text: Jewish variety of spice with tough inside

indicators.note: inside says the second piece is placed within the first
a variety of the word is a rearranged version of its letters

parts.note: hard means tough

explanation.surface: A cook adds a variety of spice with something chewy inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges the spice as SEPIC; 'inside' puts the tough word within it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sephardic describes Jews of Spanish or Portuguese descent.

clue.text: Being larger than 1 across there's room for cuts here

definitions.meaning: a playhouse with its stage is grander than the cinema screen
a hospital operating room where surgeons cut

explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is bigger than a screen, and an operating room in a hospital shares the name.

clue.text: Perturbed spirits needing time on top, including nude option

indicators.note: on means the time letter is set before the rest
including says the rearranged word is placed within the word for top

parts.note: the head is the top of something

indicators.note: an option is one alternative arrangement, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restless ghosts want time on top, with a nude option included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'option' rearranges the nude as UNDE, placed by 'including' inside the top after its second letter; 'on' sets the time first.
explanation.definitionFit: The undead are spirits that cannot rest, such as ghosts and vampires.

clue.text: Quiet quirky queer student in sort of flashback

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: quirky suggests the word queer is twisted into a new order

parts.note: L is the learner plate abbreviation for a student

explanation.surface: An odd student in a flashback scene is quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quirky' rearranges QUEER into REQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prequel shows events that happened before an earlier story, a sort of look back in time.

clue.text: Spotted one form of 9 between 5s with noughts

indicators.note: between says one piece sits between the two letters of the other

parts.note: 5 with one nought is 50, Roman L, and with two noughts 500, Roman D

indicators.note: one form of the word is a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: 9 across, the second part of a cowboy film, OPERA

explanation.surface: A spotted opera singer appears between fifty and five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one form of' rearranges 9 across as EOPAR, placed 'between' the two Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A leopard is a spotted big cat, so a spotted animal.

clue.text: See 10
Accessible file born in back seat before time

indicators.note: before puts the reversed seat ahead of the time
in says the letter for born sits inside the turned seat
back tells us to read the church seat from right to left

parts.note: a pew is a church seat
an age is a time

explanation.surface: A baby is born in the back seat before its due time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the church seat round to WEP; the born letter goes 'in' after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A web page is a document on the internet that anyone can access.

clue.text: I agree with article about myself

indicators.note: about says the article goes round the word for myself

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
me means myself

explanation.surface: I agree with the article about myself.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying amen expresses agreement, so it means I agree.

clue.text: Score more than 40, say

indicators.note: say means the letters are pronounced as spoken

parts.note: 40 in Roman numerals is XL

explanation.surface: A batsman scores more than forty runs.
explanation.walkthrough: XL spoken as letters sounds like 'excel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo or surpass others, scoring more than they do.

clue.text: Fight for chocolate cake with picture maker

parts.note: to box is to fight with fists
a brownie is a small chocolate cake

explanation.surface: Fighting for a chocolate cake with a photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Box Brownie was a simple, cheap Kodak camera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Box Brownie was a cheap Kodak camera that made photographs.

clue.text: Don't permit 11 to play a part

indicators.note: a part means only a piece of the run of words is taken

parts.note: 11 across spelt out as its answer, the short television run, followed by the words to play

explanation.surface: Stop a short television series being given a part in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out 11 across and the answer sits in 'miniseriES TO Play'. To estop is a legal term for barring someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop, in law, is to bar or preclude someone from doing something.

clue.text: God of peace?

parts.note: read as zero noise, nothing plus a racket, the Norse chief god

explanation.walkthrough: The Norse chief god was a god of war, so 'of peace' is a joke: O (nothing) plus DIN (noise) is peace.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief god of Norse mythology splits as nothing plus noise, which would be peaceful.

clue.text: Physician, posh one with a degree, one for 1 across or 22 part 1

parts.note: doc is short for doctor
U means upper class
a doctor holds a degree, DR
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A posh doctor with a degree turns up in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A docudrama is a dramatised documentary, a kind of film or television programme.

clue.text: What happens to English when blower is French

parts.note: vent is the French word for wind

explanation.surface: Something happens to an Englishman when the wind is French.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence, something that happens.

clue.text: Stop inside

definitions.meaning: part of the large intestine inside the body

explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation mark, a stop, and also part of the bowel, inside us.

clue.text: Ill and without a bit of energy, superseded and with nowhere to go?

indicators.note: ill suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are mixed up
without says a letter is removed from the word
a bit of is the first letter of energy

explanation.surface: A sick person who has run out of energy feels outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a bit of energy' removes an E from SUPERSEDED; 'Ill' rearranges the rest. The phrase is 'all dressed up and nowhere to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'all dressed up with nowhere to go' describes someone prepared for an occasion that never comes.
